text:
maria: heads up, seeing a spike of failed SCIM provisioning jobs and a bunch of SAML assertion expiries from the Azure AD App Proxy (~6177778880). 429s on /provision and intermittent KMS decrypt errors. anyone near identity? :eyes:
raj: can you paste the root cause logs + correlation id? also which env (staging/prod)?
maria: prod. grabbing relevant snippets now. sample error: `2026-03-23T14:47:12Z idp-proxy[svc]: saml: assertion expired (received at 2026-03-23T14:47:09Z, issuer ttl 10s)`
kevin: wait ttl 10s? that's tiny. Azure AD App Proxy should be issuing ~5m assertions. did we recently change role mapping or token transform? :thinking_face:
maria: we rolled a small change to the app-proxy config yesterday (rolling restart) to tweak header passthrough. no intentional TTL changes.
ops-bot: deploy succeeded: deploy/identity-app-proxy v3.4.2 -> v3.4.3 by @maria at 2026-03-22T23:10:05Z :white_check_mark:
elaine: also seeing correlated KMS decrypt failures in audit: `kms: decrypt failed: key not found` around same window. Could be key alias flip during deploy?
kevin: if the proxy's system clock is off it would make assertions look expired immediately. can you `ntpstat` the host?
sre-oncall: I'll check host NTP. running `chronyc tracking` now.
maria: attaching logs snippet (truncated):
```
[14:46:57] idp-proxy host=proxy-03 ntp_offset=+3.2s
[14:47:09] saml request id=abc123 issuer=azure-ad assertion_not_on_or_after=2026-03-23T14:47:19Z
[14:47:09] saml validation failed: current_time 2026-03-23T14:47:12Z > not_on_or_after 2026-03-23T14:47:19Z? (difference 7s)
[14:47:10] scim POST /provision -> 429 rate_limit backoff
[14:47:11] kms decrypt err key_alias=arn:aws:kms:.../redwood-prod-main: NotFound
```
raj: those lines look like a 7s skew. but why would 7s matter if ttl is minutes? the assertion_not_on_or_after is only 10s after issue per log? check the assertion issuance time vs not_on_or_after. maybe the issuer is using short ttl when proxy resubmitted assertion.
maria: azure side shows assertion created at 14:47:10 and not_on_or_after 14:47:20. so it's 10s TTL. still odd.
elaine: we had a temporary config to enforce short-lived assertions for a pilot last week; could that have leaked to prod via a malformed feature flag?
kevin: possible. also KMS NotFound suggests the proxy attempted to use a newly-rotated key alias that isn't usable yet. rotation + skew could combine to fail signature validation and decryption.
security-bot: high-priority incident created: INC-2026-0423 (identity: app-proxy assertion & provisioning failures). PagerDuty runbook linked. :rotating_light:
maria: mitigation steps I've applied: 1) rolled back app-proxy to v3.4.2 on proxy-01/02 2) scoped SCIM backoff to 2m 3) temporary allowlist for provisioning queue to prevent customer-facing 429s.
raj: good. can you also capture OS clock and `aws kms describe-key` around one of the failing times? need to see key state and alias propagation latency.
maria: did `chronyc tracking` on proxy-03: `System time correct to within 0.001s` earlier but earlier log showed +3.2s — looks like transient. also `aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/redwood-prod-main` returned key state: `PendingDeletion` at 14:46:58 then `Enabled` at 14:47:30. looks like a partial rotate during deploy window.
sre-oncall: that aligns. If the alias was briefly in PendingDeletion, decrypts would fail. combined with a pilot TTL of 10s on assertions, any small skew would trigger validation failures.
kevin: root cause hypothesis: key rotation/alias swap happened during a rolling restart; a pilot feature flag reduced assertion lifetime to 10s and leaked to prod, plus transient clock skew on proxy-03 -> combined failures (SAML expiry + KMS NotFound) -> SCIM backpressure and 429s.
elaine: next steps: 1) block accidental feature flag scope to prod 2) add guardrail to prevent KMS alias state transitions during active rolling restarts 3) add alert when assertion_ttl < 30s 4) backfill audit logs for any decryption failures (compliance).
maria: I've opened PRs for 1+3, and a runbook update for 2. I'll also open a support ticket with Azure AD to confirm why TTL was 10s for that app.
raj: for compliance, export the KMS key rotation timeline and tie to audit entries, we'll need to annotate the incident with key ARNs.
security-bot: incident severity set to P1, notify execs.
maria: temporary postmortem draft is started, tagging @elaine and @raj to help with audit writeup. thanks all :thumbsup:
